stem: The system of racial discrimination and segregation practised in South Africa was called:
solution: Apartheid was the system of legalised racial segregation and discrimination against non-whites in South Africa.

stem: The leader who fought against apartheid and became the first Black President of South Africa was:
solution: Nelson Mandela led the struggle against apartheid and became the first Black President of a democratic South Africa in 1994.

stem: Nelson Mandela spent about how many years in prison for opposing apartheid?
solution: Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison for his struggle against the apartheid regime.

stem: The party that led the anti-apartheid struggle in South Africa was the:
solution: The African National Congress (ANC) led the long struggle against apartheid in South Africa.

stem: The new democratic Constitution of South Africa was notable for its emphasis on:
options: Reconciliation, equality and the protection of all citizens' rights
solution: The South African Constitution is admired for promoting reconciliation among former enemies and guaranteeing equality and rights for all.

stem: A constitution is best described as:
options: The supreme law that lays down the framework and principles of governance
solution: A constitution is the supreme law of a country that lays down the fundamental principles and framework of its governance.

stem: The body that drafted the Constitution of India was the:
solution: The Constituent Assembly, whose members were elected by the provincial assemblies, drafted the Indian Constitution.

stem: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution was:
solution: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is regarded as the chief architect of the Constitution.

stem: The President of the Constituent Assembly of India was:
solution: Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President (Chairman) of the Constituent Assembly.

stem: The Indian Constitution was adopted on:
solution: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, now Constitution Day.

stem: The Indian Constitution came into effect on:
solution: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

stem: The introductory statement of the Constitution, expressing its ideals, is called the:
solution: The Preamble is the opening statement that sets out the guiding values and objectives of the Constitution.

stem: According to the Preamble, India is a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic:
solution: The Preamble declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.

stem: In the Preamble, 'Sovereign' means that India:
options: Is free to take its own decisions, internal and external
solution: 'Sovereign' means India is an independent country, free to take its own decisions without external control.

stem: In the Preamble, 'Republic' means that:
options: The head of state is elected, not a hereditary monarch
solution: 'Republic' means the head of state (the President) is elected and not a hereditary ruler.

stem: The values that guided the making of the Indian Constitution came largely from:
options: The ideals of the national/freedom movement
solution: The Constitution's guiding values grew out of the ideals and experiences of the Indian freedom struggle.

stem: The 'Objectives Resolution', outlining the ideals of the Constitution, was moved by:
solution: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution, which laid out the ideals and objectives of the Constitution.

stem: The Constitution of India draws upon the experiences of:
options: Many countries and India's own freedom struggle
solution: The framers studied the constitutions and experiences of many countries and drew on India's own freedom struggle.

stem: The word 'Secular' in the Preamble means that the state:
options: Treats all religions equally and has no official religion
solution: 'Secular' means the state treats all religions equally and does not adopt any official religion.

stem: The Constitution promises its citizens Justice, Liberty, Equality and:
solution: The Preamble promises Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity to all citizens.

stem: 'Fraternity' in the Preamble refers to:
options: A sense of brotherhood and unity among all citizens
solution: 'Fraternity' means a spirit of brotherhood and unity that treats all citizens as members of one family.

stem: The making of the Indian Constitution took about:
solution: The Constituent Assembly took nearly three years (1946-1949) to draft and adopt the Constitution.

stem: One reason the Indian Constitution has been widely accepted is that it was:
options: Made through a broadly representative and deliberative process
solution: The Constitution's acceptance owes much to the broadly representative and deliberative process by which it was made.

stem: The Preamble begins with the words:
solution: The Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India', showing that the Constitution derives its authority from the people.

stem: 'We, the people of India' in the Preamble signifies that the ultimate authority rests with:
solution: The phrase signifies that the Constitution's authority flows from the people of India themselves.

stem: The example of South Africa's constitution shows that a constitution can help:
options: Former enemies live together as equals and build trust
solution: South Africa's constitution demonstrates how a constitution can help former enemies reconcile and live together as equal citizens.

stem: The Constituent Assembly members were:
options: Elected mainly by the members of the provincial assemblies
solution: The Constituent Assembly's members were elected mainly by the elected members of the provincial legislative assemblies.

stem: The Constitution provides the basic framework that decides:
options: How the government will be formed, its powers and citizens' rights
solution: The Constitution sets out how the government is formed, distributes and limits powers, and guarantees citizens' rights.

stem: A constitution generates a degree of trust among people because it:
options: Lays down agreed rules that everyone accepts
solution: A constitution builds trust by laying down agreed-upon rules that all sections of society accept and can rely on.

stem: The Indian Constitution balances the powers of government by:
options: Distributing power among organs and levels and guaranteeing rights
Concentrating all power in one person
solution: The Constitution distributes power among the legislature, executive and judiciary and across levels of government, and guarantees rights.

stem: The values enshrined in the Constitution serve as:
options: Guiding principles for the working of the government
solution: The constitutional values (justice, liberty, equality, fraternity) serve as guiding principles for how the government should function.

stem: Which of the following is a reason the framers wanted the Constitution to protect rights?
options: To prevent the misuse of power and protect minorities
solution: The framers guaranteed rights to prevent the misuse of power and to protect citizens, especially minorities.

stem: The Indian Constitution can be described as a __________ document, capable of being amended.
solution: The Constitution is a 'living document' — it can be amended to meet changing needs while retaining its basic framework.

stem: The Preamble reflects the __________ of the Constitution.
solution: The Preamble reflects the underlying philosophy and core values of the Constitution.

stem: A key lesson from South Africa's transition is that the design of a constitution requires:
options: Compromise, trust-building and agreed rules acceptable to all
solution: South Africa shows that a good constitution is built through compromise and trust, with rules acceptable to all groups.

stem: The Indian Constitution guarantees rights that are:
options: Enforceable and protected by the courts
solution: The Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Constitution are enforceable and protected by the courts.

stem: The Constituent Assembly worked through detailed discussions in order to:
options: Consider different viewpoints and build broad agreement
solution: The Constituent Assembly deliberated in detail to consider different viewpoints and build broad agreement on the Constitution.

stem: Which of the following was a prominent member of the Constituent Assembly?
solution: Prominent members of the Constituent Assembly included Jawaharlal Nehru, B. R. Ambedkar, Sardar Patel, Rajendra Prasad and others.

stem: The Constitution's design ensures that the government is:
options: Democratic, accountable and bound by the rule of law
solution: The constitutional design ensures a democratic, accountable government bound by the rule of law.

stem: The experience of both South Africa and India shows that constitutions are made especially at moments of:
options: Major political transition (like the birth of a new nation or democracy)
solution: Constitutions are often framed at moments of major political transition, such as the birth of a new nation or democracy.

stem: The authority and legitimacy of the Indian Constitution rest on the fact that it:
options: Was drawn up by representatives of the people through a legitimate process
solution: The Constitution's legitimacy rests on its having been framed by the people's representatives through a legitimate, deliberative process.

stem: The core function of a constitution is to:
options: Set out the fundamental rules and values by which a country is governed
solution: A constitution's core function is to lay down the fundamental rules and values by which a country is governed.

stem: The Indian Constitution reflects a commitment to:
options: Democracy, equality, liberty, secularism and justice
solution: The Constitution reflects a commitment to democracy, equality, liberty, secularism, justice and fraternity.

stem: The making of a constitution through consensus, as in India and South Africa, helps ensure that it is:
solution: Building a constitution through consensus makes it widely accepted and durable.

stem: The Preamble can be seen as the __________ of the Constitution.
solution: The Preamble is often described as the soul or guiding spirit of the Constitution, summarising its ideals.

stem: The struggle against apartheid teaches that constitutional design must protect:
options: The rights and dignity of all, including former oppressed groups
solution: The anti-apartheid struggle teaches that a constitution must protect the rights and dignity of all, especially previously oppressed groups.

stem: The Indian Constitution is one of the __________ written constitutions in the world.
solution: The Indian Constitution is one of the longest and most detailed written constitutions in the world.

stem: The values in the Preamble are meant to be:
options: The guiding ideals that shape laws and government action
solution: The Preamble's values are meant to guide the making of laws and the actions of the government.

stem: The Constitution of India drew several structural/administrative features from which colonial-era law?
solution: Many administrative and structural provisions of the Constitution were adapted from the Government of India Act, 1935.

stem: The Constituent Assembly that framed the Indian Constitution held its first meeting in:
solution: The Constituent Assembly first met in December 1946, and, after Partition, reassembled as the Constituent Assembly of India to draft the Constitution.

stem: The Indian Constitution took how long to be framed?
solution: The Constituent Assembly took precisely two years, eleven months and eighteen days to complete the making of the Constitution.

stem: The 'Objectives Resolution', which laid down the ideals and guiding principles of the Constitution, was moved by:
solution: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution in December 1946, outlining the aims and objectives that later shaped the Preamble.

stem: The system of racial segregation in South Africa in which people were classified and separated by their race was called:
solution: Apartheid was the official policy of racial separation and discrimination followed by the white minority government in South Africa.

stem: Under apartheid in South Africa, people were divided and labelled on the basis of their skin colour into groups such as white, black, coloured and:
solution: The apartheid regime classified the population by race into white, black, coloured (mixed race) and Indian, granting rights unequally.

stem: The African National Congress (ANC) led the struggle against apartheid; its most famous leader who became the first President of democratic South Africa was:
solution: Nelson Mandela led the anti-apartheid movement as a leader of the ANC and became the first President of a democratic South Africa in 1994.

stem: Nelson Mandela spent about how many years in prison for his fight against apartheid?
solution: Nelson Mandela was sentenced to life imprisonment and spent 28 years in a South African prison, mostly on Robben Island, before his release in 1990.

stem: Apartheid in South Africa formally came to an end and a new democratic government was formed in the year:
solution: On 26 April 1994, the new national flag of a democratic South Africa was unfurled, marking the birth of a new democracy after apartheid ended.

stem: The new Constitution of democratic South Africa is admired especially because it:
options: Guarantees to its citizens the most extensive rights available in any country
solution: The South African Constitution is admired the world over for giving its citizens the most extensive rights and for the way it was negotiated between former enemies.

stem: The negotiations that led to South Africa's new constitution took place between the ANC and the:
solution: After years of oppression, the ANC and the white regime negotiated together to draw up a common constitution, showing that former enemies could agree on shared rules.

stem: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
solution: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (now celebrated as Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.

stem: The Constitution of India came into force on:
solution: The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day, marking India's transition to a republic.

stem: The date 26 January was chosen for the Constitution to come into force because it commemorated the:
solution: 26 January was chosen because on that day in 1930 the Indian National Congress had declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as its goal.

stem: Which of the following words was NOT part of the original 1950 Preamble but was added later by the 42nd Amendment (1976)?
solution: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976; the original Preamble described India as Sovereign, Democratic Republic.

stem: In the Preamble, the word 'Sovereign' means that India:
options: Is free to take its own decisions, internal and external, without outside interference
Is ruled by the United Nations
solution: 'Sovereign' means the people of India have supreme power to take their own decisions on internal and external matters, free from any external control.

stem: In the Preamble, 'Secular' means that:
options: Citizens have complete freedom to follow any religion and the state treats all religions equally
The state has an official religion
solution: 'Secular' means citizens have complete freedom to follow any religion, and the state does not favour or discriminate against any religion.

stem: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution begins with the words:
solution: The Preamble opens with 'We, the People of India', signifying that the Constitution derives its authority from the people of India.

stem: The phrase 'We, the People of India' in the Preamble indicates that the Constitution:
options: Was drawn up and enacted by the people of India through their representatives
Was written by the President alone
solution: 'We, the People of India' shows that the ultimate authority behind the Constitution rests with the people, who enacted it through the Constituent Assembly.

stem: The Constitution declares four kinds of Justice/values in the Preamble: Justice, Liberty, Equality and:
solution: The Preamble secures to all citizens Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity — the four foundational values of the Constitution.

stem: The parliamentary form of government in the Indian Constitution was largely inspired by the practice in:
solution: The framers borrowed the parliamentary form of government and the idea of a nominal head from the British system.

stem: The idea of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution was inspired mainly by the constitution of:
solution: The concept of justiciable Fundamental Rights (Bill of Rights) was drawn from the Constitution of the United States of America.

stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the constitution of:
solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which had in turn borrowed the idea from Spain.

stem: The framers of the Indian Constitution drew upon the experience of:
options: Constitutions of many countries as well as India's own freedom struggle
solution: The makers of the Constitution studied the constitutions of many countries and combined those ideas with lessons from India's freedom struggle to create a document suited to Indian conditions.

stem: Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution enjoys wide acceptance and legitimacy. Reason (R): It was framed through detailed discussion and broad consensus in the Constituent Assembly.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: The Constitution commands respect because it was made after careful deliberation and consensus among representatives of diverse groups — R explains A.

stem: Which prominent leader, a woman social reformer, was among the members of the Constituent Assembly?
solution: The Constituent Assembly included prominent figures such as Sarojini Naidu, Hansa Mehta and Durgabai Deshmukh among its women members.

stem: The Constituent Assembly of India was constituted mainly under the:
solution: The Constituent Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, with members elected indirectly by the provincial assemblies.

stem: One important function of a constitution is that it:
options: Specifies how the government will be constituted and limits its powers
solution: A constitution lays out how the government will be formed, who will have the power to make decisions, and imposes limits on the powers of the government to protect citizens' rights.

stem: A constitution generates a degree of trust and coordination among people because it:
options: Sets out agreed-upon rules that everyone can rely on
solution: A constitution provides a set of basic rules that allow minimal coordination and generate trust among members of a society who may not fully agree on everything else.

stem: The making of the constitutions of both India and South Africa shows that a good constitution is best made through:
solution: Both the Indian and South African constitutions were made through negotiation and consensus among diverse groups, which is why they are widely accepted and durable.

stem: The Preamble is often described as the __________ of the Constitution because it captures its guiding ideals.
solution: The Preamble is called the soul or philosophy of the Constitution, as it embodies the fundamental values and objectives on which the Constitution is based.

stem: The Indian Constitution is often described as one of the:
options: Longest written constitutions in the world
solution: The Indian Constitution is one of the longest and most detailed written constitutions in the world, reflecting the diversity and complexity of the country.

stem: Match the value with its meaning: (i) Liberty (ii) Equality (iii) Fraternity — (a) equal status and opportunity (b) freedom of thought and expression (c) brotherhood among all:
solution: Liberty means freedom of thought, expression and belief; Equality means equal status and opportunity; Fraternity means brotherhood and dignity of the individual.

stem: The lesson from South Africa's transition to democracy is that a constitution must:
options: Build trust between former enemies and protect the rights of all groups
solution: South Africa's negotiated constitution showed that constitutional design must accommodate the interests of all groups and build trust, so that even former oppressors and oppressed could live together under agreed rules.

stem: The values that guided the framing of the Indian Constitution came largely from:
options: The ideals of the national/freedom movement
solution: The values enshrined in the Constitution — like liberty, equality, secularism and social justice — grew out of the ideals of India's freedom struggle and were shared by the makers of the Constitution.

stem: The Indian Constitution provides for a division of powers among the legislature, executive and judiciary in order to:
options: Prevent any one organ from becoming too powerful
solution: By distributing power among the legislature, executive and judiciary, the Constitution ensures a system of checks and balances so that no single organ can misuse power.

stem: Assertion (A): The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' appear in the present Preamble. Reason (R): They were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 — R correctly explains why they are present in the current Preamble.

stem: The Constitution's guarantee that its ideals cannot be easily changed by any government reflects the idea that the Constitution is:
options: The supreme law, above ordinary laws and governments
solution: The Constitution is the supreme law; governments and their laws must operate within its framework, and its basic ideals cannot be overridden by ordinary legislation.

stem: The Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru later formed the basis of the:
solution: The ideals expressed in Nehru's Objectives Resolution were later incorporated into the Preamble of the Constitution.

stem: The Indian national flag of democratic South Africa comparison highlights that both countries:
options: Emerged from struggles against injustice and adopted democratic constitutions
solution: Both India (against colonial rule) and South Africa (against apartheid) emerged from struggles against injustice and chose to be governed by democratic constitutions rooted in equality and rights.

stem: Which of the following best states why a country needs a constitution?
options: To lay down agreed rules, allocate power, limit government, and protect citizens' rights
solution: A constitution is needed to express trust and coordination, specify how power is distributed and exercised, set limits on the government, and enshrine the rights and aspirations of the people.

stem: The Constituent Assembly worked mainly through committees and detailed debates because the framers wanted the Constitution to:
options: Reflect wide agreement and careful thought
solution: Each clause was discussed threadbare in committees and open debate, so that the Constitution would command consensus and legitimacy across India's diverse society.

stem: The image of Nelson Mandela and the ANC negotiating with the white regime is used in the chapter to teach that:
options: Even bitter opponents can agree on constitutional rules for living together
solution: South Africa shows that a constitution can be built by former enemies who agree to certain basic rules, enabling different groups to live together peacefully.

stem: The overall theme of 'Constitutional Design' is how:
options: Countries like India and South Africa framed constitutions embodying democratic values after major transitions
One person should design the constitution
solution: The chapter explains how nations like India and South Africa designed constitutions embodying democratic values and rights after major political transitions.
